items.note: Story 1: 'In January 1925 they petitioned' — the petition date carries the item on its own.
Alonzo Frick chairman of a board of three; sat 17 March at Ashlin, twice in April in the station's weigh room, closed 4 May 1925 — three sessions, two in the weigh room.
'water (Vose), cream theft (Teague), wet hay (the 1908 report read in) — and none accepted.'

'Before it were four books only': test book, receiving book, Brant's weigh book, Strawn's 1923 notebook (Exhibit 4); Story 1 also notes nobody connected the condemnation with twenty-six years of low tests.
Put out 30 April 1925 by letter; 4 May 'no cause established' and $3,800 'without admission', charged to the station account.

Story 2: 'The $3,800 award had been a fifth of it' ($19,000 from the ledger sum); Story 1 charges the award to the station account and Story 2 sums the station-gain entries over 1898-1922. The identity of the two accounts is left implicit, but every element sits inside this batch's Section A.
Ivy Keddie, born 1931, Ansel's granddaughter (Duncan's daughter), graduate student in dairy husbandry at the State Agricultural College, Farland; Professor Leland Vaught.
'laid side by side what nobody had': test book, Roy's weigh book, Rosalie's Alder Corners table, Strawn's volume, the annual ledgers.
February 1958, the loft over the old station's intake room, nine pipettes unbroken.
9 March, calibrated burette, 16.70-16.74, mean 16.72 against 17.6 — short 0.88 c.c., 95 hundredths of the mark.
'3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80; the gap of 0.19 was one-twentieth of the true test' — 0.19 given as proportional, not a constant; span bounded by 1898-1922 / twenty-six years / 12 June 1923 in Story 1.

All four required elements inside Section A: 40,000,000 lb over twenty-five years (Story 1), 76,000 lb, $19,000 at 25 cents, and the identity with the summed 'station gain' entries 1898-1922 (Story 2).
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, quoted; 'Thirty-five years from glass to cause, thirty-three from dismissal' and 'twenty-four years after his death'.

Bucket maxed. Correctly resolved with a stated method: weigh-book start 1 Jan 1897 (exhibit list), Orra's birth 1866 (arithmetic on 'eighty-two in 1948'), crate found in the station loft (Nym's catalogue slip), Selby manager 1913, sixteen Alder Corners seasons, 1908 committee not the 1925 board, condemnation 12 June 1923 (the 28 June order), 1908 sampling Jan-Mar, and more.

Bucket maxed. Twenty pairs listed with breakers, including NT-1 (16.27, Vaught + Chronicle, broken by the nine listed readings and the 0.95 ratio), NT-11 (12 July, broken by the 28 June order), NT-14 ($77.39, broken by summing Junia's own facsimile), NT-16 (eleven pipettes), NT-15 (five dozen), NT-18 (great-niece), NT-23 (Strawn from 1908).

A04 earned (#53 'not provable', with what the sources do establish); A10 earned (#58 'cannot be settled; the pamphlet is undated and the 1889-92 minute book lost'). A06 LOST: #5 settles the 1911 borrowed measure on 'Larrow Green', treating the elimination of the state-man pole as a settlement — exactly what the key's grader note forbids.

Part C lists sixteen self-refutations, several from the key's list (Junia's $77.93 facsimile beside '$77.39' and 'nothing before 1900' beside an 1897 invoice; Grigg's 'whole of 1908'; Duncan's 1868 against 'eighty-two in 1948'; Vaught's 16.27/118,000 against his own section VII; Keddie's Ashlin creamery). Buckets sum to 9; section capped at 8.

Names the 1897 Ammon pipettes at 16.72 against 17.6, derives 0.95 and 0.19 as five percent of 3.80 and explicitly proportional, and gives onset (1 May 1897; 1896 borrowed glass at 3.80) and cessation (12 June 1923; 1924 at 3.80) with nothing changing on the farms.
Watering named (Selby Vose's 1919 circular and 1926 address, echoed by Sill) and defeated with the lactometer visits, the Alder Corners cheese, the flat gap, the 1911 weeks and the heavy cream.
Theft named (Teague at the hearing, Rundle, Vira, Cleve's father) and defeated with the ledger's heavy cream in the accuser's own hand, the 1911 interval and the 1923-24 rise under the same tester.
Bog hay named (Grigg's 1908 committee, Kepp, Falke's withdrawn draft) and defeated with Bulletin 214's five hundredths in winter and nothing in summer, the flat gap, and the Alder Corners figures.

ABSTENTION A07 asserted. The passage opens 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.' and closes 'never looked at, or asked for, the glass itself' — a headline verdict sentence in the sheet's own voice.
ABSTENTION A05 correctly declined: 'whether he privately blamed the glass or the patrons cannot be determined', with the leaning toward the glass explicitly marked as inference.
151 words by a plain word count (155 whitespace tokens less three em-dashes and the ampersand) — one over the 150-word cap.
Names seven record series: test book, weigh book, ledgers, cheese-factory book, inspector's notebook, invoice, committee report and bulletin, plus the 1958 measurement.
Water, theft and wet hay appear only as what 'were blamed'; headline numbers all correct (16.72 against 17.6, 3.61 for 3.80, one part in twenty). No corrupted figure.

Four of the six arc elements covering both ends: one part in twenty and 1897 at the onset, 1923 and 1958 at the close. Ansel Keddie is named but Ivy is only 'his granddaughter', so the names element fails; the item still clears its four.

deductions.reason: Gullibility, A06: E1 item 5 asserts the 1911 borrowed measure came from Larrow Green by the cream wagon, treating the elimination of r09's pole as a settlement. The sources cannot name the lender.

Gullibility, A07: F1's subsidiary answer opens with the verdict 'No' on whether the 1925 board examined the condemned glassware and concludes the board 'never looked at, or asked for, the glass itself'.

Corruption, NT-23 (Strawn's circuit from 1908): F1 asserts 'Strawn's lactometer at every visit, 1908-1936' as fact, though E1 item 24 and Part B item 17 resolve the start correctly to 1907. Unhedged assertion of a catalogued planted value.

Corruption, X34 (the cheese factory built in 1913): E1 item 46 asserts 'Built 1913 (Rosalie) vs opened 1914 (Roy; Rundle) - reconcilable', adopting the planted 1913 as fact rather than resolving to 1914 or declaring the pair unreconcilable.
